```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Load libs
libs <- c("tidyverse","psych","ggeffects","sjPlot","lme4","car","emmeans","scales",
  "GGally","stargazer","broom","lmtest","sandwich","ggpubr","performance",
  "broom.mixed","gt","lmerTest","DataCombine","MuMIn","gtsummary","ggrepel",
  "corrplot","writexl","forcats","RColorBrewer","lubridate", "visreg"
  )
invisible(lapply(libs, require, character.only = TRUE))
options(scipen = 999, digits = 2)
options(scipen=999)
options(digits=5)

df <- read_csv("/Users/tur61139/Documents/GitHub/grant-submissions/2025_R03-SDOH/derivatives/scoring-mastersheet-SDOH.csv")

# Convert categorical vars to factors with clear references
df <- df |>
  mutate(
    demo_gender = factor(demo_gender,
                         levels = c(2, 1, 3, 4),
                         labels = c("Female", "Male", "NonBinary", "Other")),
    demo_quota = factor(demo_quota,
                        levels = c(1, 2, 3),
                        labels = c("Urban", "Suburban", "Rural")),
    # Numeric for race group
    race_group = case_when(
      demo_race == 5 ~ "White",
      demo_race == 4 ~ "Black",
      demo_race %in% c(1, 2, 3, 6, 7) ~ "Other",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    race_group = factor(race_group, levels = c("White", "Black", "Other")), 
    # Numeric for race group (two only)
    race_group2 = case_when(
      demo_race == 5 ~ "White",
      demo_race %in% c(1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7) ~ "Non-White",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    race_group2 = factor(race_group2, levels = c("White", "Non-White"))
  )
```
# Summary statistics
```{r}
summary_stats <- df |>
  mutate(across(c(demo_gender, ses_thi, demo_quota, demo_race), as.character)) |>  # ensure all are same type
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(demo_gender, ses_thi, demo_quota, demo_race),
    names_to = "dimension",
    values_to = "category"
  ) |>
  group_by(dimension, category) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    percent = round(100 * n / nrow(df), 1),
    mean_fevs = mean(fevs_total, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_fevs = sd(fevs_total, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(dimension, desc(n))
summary_stats
```
# Basic gender, race, income, location differences between groups for FEVS
``` {r, fig.height = 20, fig.width = 20, dpi = 300}
# Gender difference 
t_gender <- t.test(fevs_total ~ demo_gender, data = df)
t_gender

# t(506) = -1.69, p = .092. Good enough to show some difference/"trending", men have higher FEVS score. 

# Race difference, ANOVA - Black > White is significant, p > .001 (when demo_race is factor)
df$factor_race <- as.factor(df$demo_race)
aov_race <- aov(fevs_total ~ factor_race, data = df)
summary(aov_race)
TukeyHSD(aov_race)
# Issues with not enough subjects that are non-black or non-white (amend version); Black > White, p > .01
aov_race2 <- aov(fevs_total ~ race_group, data = df)
summary(aov_race2)
TukeyHSD(aov_race2)

t_race <- t.test(fevs_total ~ race_group2, data = df)
t_race


# Non-white subjects have a significantly higher FEVS score than white subjects, t(479) = -3.96, p > .001. 



# Income difference (ANOVA), Lvl 5 ($101,000-$150,000) > Lvl 1 ($0-$25,000) is significant, p = .02
aov_income <- aov(fevs_total ~ factor(ses_thi), data = df)
summary(aov_income)
TukeyHSD(aov_income)

# Let's break down income into high/low, $75k cutoff...
df <- df |>
  mutate(
    income_group = ifelse(ses_thi <= 3, "Low_Income", "High_Income"),
    income_group = factor(income_group, levels = c("Low_Income", "High_Income"))
  )
t_income <- t.test(fevs_total ~ income_group, data = df)
t_income # Significant, p = .002

# Location difference (ANOVA) - No sig., trending ? p = .11
aov_loc <- aov(fevs_total ~ demo_quota, data = df)
summary(aov_loc)

# Gender difference ttest -  NO DIFFERENCE
t_gender <- t.test(fevs_total ~ demo_gender, data = df)
t_gender
summary(lm(fevs_total ~ demo_gender, data = df))

# Race difference, ANOVA - Black > White is significant, p > .001 (when demo_race is factor)
df$factor_race <- as.factor(df$demo_race)
aov_race <- aov(fevs_total ~ factor_race, data = df)
summary(aov_race)
TukeyHSD(aov_race)
# Issues with not enough subjects that are non-black or non-white (amend version); Black > White, p > .01
aov_race2 <- aov(fevs_total ~ race_group, data = df)
summary(aov_race2)
TukeyHSD(aov_race2)

aov_race3 <- aov(fevs_total ~ race_group2, data = df)
summary(aov_race3)
TukeyHSD(aov_race3)

# Income difference (ANOVA), Lvl 5 ($101,000-$150,000) > Lvl 1 ($0-$25,000) is significant, p = .02
aov_income <- aov(fevs_total ~ factor(ses_thi), data = df)
summary(aov_income)
TukeyHSD(aov_income)

# Let's break down income into high/low, $75k cutoff...
df <- df |>
  mutate(
    income_group = ifelse(ses_thi <= 3, "Low_Income", "High_Income"),
    income_group = factor(income_group, levels = c("Low_Income", "High_Income"))
  )
t_income <- t.test(fevs_total ~ income_group, data = df)
t_income # Significant, p = .002

# Location difference (ANOVA) - No sig., trending ? p = .11
aov_loc <- aov(fevs_total ~ demo_quota, data = df)
summary(aov_loc)

df$demo_quota <- relevel(df$demo_quota, ref = "Suburban")
summary(lm(fevs_total ~ demo_quota, data = df))

#

summ <- \(d,g) d |>
  filter(!is.na(.data[[g]]), !is.na(fevs_total)) |>
  group_by(.data[[g]]) |>
  summarise(n=n(), mean=mean(fevs_total),
            se=sd(fevs_total)/sqrt(n),
            low=mean-1.96*se, high=mean+1.96*se, .groups="drop") |>
  rename(group=!!g)

# Function to make bar plots with p-value label or significance asterisk
pb <- \(s, xlab, pval, pcols = NULL) {
  label <- paste0("p = ", formatC(pval, format = "f", digits = 3))
  ggplot(s, aes(group, mean, fill = group)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.7, color = "black") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = low, ymax = high), width = 0.18) +
    geom_text(aes(y = high, label = paste0("N=", n)), vjust = -0.6, size = 3) +
    annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, label = label,
             hjust = 1.05, vjust = 2, size = 3.5, fontface = "italic") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pcols) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = "FEVS Score (mean and 95% CI)") +
    guides(fill = "none") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 20) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 6)))
}

# Summaries
s_gender <- summ(df |> filter(demo_gender %in% c("Female","Male")), "demo_gender")
s_race3  <- summ(df, "race_group2")
s_inc    <- summ(df, "income_group")
s_loc    <- summ(df, "demo_quota")

# Colors
cols_gender <- c("Female"="coral1","Male"="turquoise3")
cols_race   <- c("White"="skyblue","Non-White"="green4")
cols_inc    <- c("Low_Income"="gold2","High_Income"="dodgerblue")
cols_loc    <- c("Urban"="blue","Suburban"="maroon","Rural"="yellowgreen")

# p-values from your already-run tests
p_gender <- t_gender$p.value
p_race3  <- summary(aov_race3)[[1]][["Pr(>F)"]][1]
p_income <- t_income$p.value
p_loc    <- summary(aov_loc)[[1]][["Pr(>F)"]][1]

# Build plots
p1 <- pb(s_gender, "Gender (Female vs Male)", p_gender, cols_gender)
p2 <- pb(s_race3,  "Race (White vs Non-White)", p_race3, cols_race)
p3 <- pb(s_inc,    "Income (less than $75k vs $75k or more)", p_income, cols_inc)
p4 <- pb(s_loc,    "Region (Urban/Suburban/Rural)", p_loc, cols_loc)

# Combine
p_all <- ggarrange(p1, p2, p3, p4, ncol=2, nrow=2, labels="AUTO")
p_all <- annotate_figure(p_all,
  top=text_grob("FEVS by Demographic", face="bold", size=22)
)
p_all
```
